name: Tang Xianzu
credit: Portrait of Tang Xianzu (湯顯祖), Ming-period · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Tang Xianzu (湯顯祖, courtesy name Yireng, 1550–1616) was a Ming-dynasty playwright and poet from Linchuan in Jiangxi. He took the jinshi degree in 1583 and served in Nanjing, but his outspoken memorial of 1591 criticising the court led to his banishment to Guangdong; after a spell as magistrate of Suichang he resigned in 1598 and spent his last years at home, writing in his studio, the Jade Tea Hall (玉茗堂).

His four dramas, the Four Dreams of the Jade Tea Hall, include The Peony Pavilion (牡丹亭, also called 還魂記), a long chuanqi play of fifty-five scenes in sung verse and speech, about a young woman who dies of love for a man she has met only in a dream and is brought back to life. It is the best known of all Chinese dramas of the Ming period.
